channel.title: Twinthos field notes
channel.description: AI security, agents and practical automation.

item.title: Before you give an agent access.
item.description: Questions that turn an impressive demonstration into a reviewable deployment.

item.title: AI agents in 2027: trust is the infrastructure.
item.description: The next wave of AI will act inside businesses. Its identity, permissions and evidence will matter as much as its intelligence.

item.title: Memory needs ownership, too.
item.description: A Company Brain is useful when its knowledge is current, attributable and available to the right people.

item.title: What an agent actually does.
item.description: The useful difference is the ability to move from a request to a tool action and a checked result.

item.title: The failure behind the successful demo.
item.description: A demonstration follows a clean path. Real work includes missing data, expired access and contradictory instructions.

item.title: From conversation to responsibility.
item.description: A digital employee is a service role for software. The name matters less than the job, tools and accountability.

item.title: AI, without the fog.
item.description: A practical vocabulary for deciding what belongs in your business.

item.title: Price the work, not the label.
item.description: A way to compare a managed AI service without inventing savings.

item.title: The costs around the model.
item.description: Model usage is one line in a wider operating budget.

item.title: The first job to hand over.
item.description: Small businesses can start with a manageable workflow instead of a company-wide transformation.

item.title: What an AI phone service really costs.
item.description: A cheap headline rate does not describe a complete telephone workflow.

item.title: Automation changes the shape of a job.
item.description: Historical analogies can start a discussion. They cannot forecast your staffing needs.

item.title: Superintelligence is not a deployment plan.
item.description: Future capability is a different question from what your system can safely do today.
